turns.message: Hey Royce, it's Co. Any luck finding another sponsor for the event since Civic Joy Fund fell through?

Yeah. No, we're, um, we're actually canceling the event. Um, so that's out the window for this time around. Uh, our focus is partnering with another startup called Sequent AI, um, later on in November. So I'll hope focus on that. Uh, so we can kind of forget about October, um, date since it's already SF Tech Week. We didn't want to spend unnecessary money, so.
Got it—so the October push is off, and you're shifting to November with Sequent AI instead. That makes sense given the timing and the money piece.
What's the shape of that partnership looking like—is this an event you're running together, or something else?

Yeah, so he's throwing a launch party for his, his startup, so he asked us to kind of partner with us. Jacqueline, my co-founder, actually spearheaded that, and I set, set up the meeting between those two because I was unable to. Um, we haven't looked at, you know, the specifics around it yet, um, but we actually want to keep that relationship warm, so we're just thinking about inviting him out to dinner, maybe a business lunch, and see where we could kind of cross paths along the way.
So Jacqueline's leading that one, and you're playing a longer game with it—building the relationship first before you nail down what the event actually is. That's smart.
Where are you at now with the first paying customer piece—that still the move, or has that shifted too?
What do you mean by first paying customer? Like, um, putting the actual product out there? I'm confused on what you mean. I don't know.

Yeah, that's on me—I had a note that you were figuring out how to get your first paying customer or check for Co, but I realize I don't actually know what that means in your world. What does that look like for you?
What are you talking about?

I think I got something wrong on my end. Let me back up—what I had was that you were working toward getting a first paying customer for Co, but I realize I don't actually know what shape that takes for you or if that's even the right way to say it. What's actually happening on that front?

Yeah. I mean, we're still in the, the development phase. Like, you know, I've been building you out and making sure code is, you know, designed correctly. You know, every time we kind of-- Or every time I start coding, like, it just seems like it's just new things that pop up that needs to be, you know, closed within the gap. Um, so that's where we are. We haven't pushed in production yet, which we probably start n- n- need- needing to. But, um, yeah, that's where we're at so far.

So you're still deep in the build, and every time you think you're close, there's another gap that needs closing. When you do push to production, what does that first version need to look like—or are you still figuring that out?

Uh, we're still figuring that out. That's more so, you know, we're connecting inside the room. So basically, we're gonna use more so app clips to kind of help us put that along, string that together. And, you know, honestly, I would love to-- for you to, like, kind of lead that front and help us... Well, not that part, but I would want you to help us lead into this partnership with Sequent AI and kind of see, you know, what notes you could possibly, you know, generate for us and alignment, you know, that you could see that we could have with that company. Um, from my forefront, I'm thinking already off the back, like, hey,why don't we power your guest list, have people match inside the room seamlessly, and, you know, have a, you know, maybe a, a minute, five-minute conversation with you to be paired with other folks in the room?

So you want me to dig into Sequent AI—what they're building, who they're targeting, what their launch looks like—and come back with specific alignment points and maybe a sharper pitch for how Co could actually work in that room. That's doable. I'll set that up when we hang up and text you what I find.

The five-minute conversation piece is interesting—that's you solving for the cold-start problem at the event itself. You already thinking about how that actually works, or is that still forming?
Still ...
Um, how would you do it?

The five minutes before the event starts—that's when you'd do it. Get people in early, have them do a quick intro with you or Jacqueline on video or voice, just enough to know who they are and what they're looking for. Then when the room opens, you've already got those notes, and matching happens fast instead of cold.

Or you do it as people arrive, first thing, before they hit the main room. Either way, you're gathering signal before the mingling starts so the pairing isn't just random.

What's your instinct on timing—before they get there, or right as they walk in?

Uh, we kind of want to do a hybrid of both. Like, we would love to kind of have that be a gateway into actually attending the event. Like, "Hey, talk to our AI, get a picture, um, deeply understand who you are," because that leads to better matching. Inside the event, you know, we wouldn't press the situation. We'll have them actually text you and be like, "Hey, you know, such and such is what I'm looking for," and you match them based on that. But I feel like as they talk to you, they will have a stronger match.

That's smart—you're using the conversation as a filter and a signal generator at the same time. They get value out of it (understanding who they are, a picture), you get what you need to actually make good matches, and it feels natural, not transactional.

So the gateway piece is real—they're not getting in the room without that conversation, which means you control the quality of who's there and what you know about them going in. Then inside, they text you when they want an intro, and you've already got the depth.

What happens if someone shows up and doesn't want to do the conversation first—do they still get in, or is that the actual gate?
Uh, I don't know. What do you think?

[thoughtful] Make it the gate. If you let people skip it, you lose the signal, and then your matches are worse, and the whole thing falls apart. The conversation is what makes Co actually work in that room—it's not a nice-to-have, it's the thing that lets you do what you said you'd do.

Frame it right and people won't resist it. It's not "answer questions before you can come," it's "talk to Co so we can actually introduce you to people worth meeting instead of leaving you to work the room blind."
Yeah, you're right about that.
So that's locked. Anything else you're working through on the Sequent side, or is that the shape of it for now?

That's the shape of it for now. Uh, what I actually want you to do, I want you to put together a, like a PDF for me, um, and just what you started noticing, what we kind of described today. It doesn't have to be verbatim, but just a summary of where we're gonna start, our goal as far as Sequent AI, and what do you think, uh, we should be able to funnel inside the room, and how we'll be able to find, uh, funnel inside the room. So those are the things I want you to work on.

Got it. I'll put together a PDF after we hang up—the shape of the partnership, what you're after with Sequent, how the gateway conversation works, and what you're actually funneling into the room. I'll text it to you when it's done.

Anything else on your plate right now, or is that the main thing?

No, that's pretty much it. You know, today was a long day. Um, just kind of tired and drained. Um, ultimately, we'll be open to this weekend just to kick back and relax, if you could find something there for me. Um, just want to focus more on my, like, my mental health.

[softly] A long day like that will drain you. This weekend sounds like what you need right now.

I've got a few things on file from what we're looking for—there's a dance workshop Saturday afternoon with a BlackPink choreographer, nothing heavy, just builders in a room having fun. And Sunday there's a low-pressure fair in Oakland, come and go as you like, 25+ local groups. Both are the opposite of networking—just room to be around people without any performance expected. Want me to text you those links, or are...
Yeah, just send, just send those over.

Done. I'll text them to you right after we hang up.

You've got a lot moving—the build, the Sequent piece, and now you need to actually breathe this weekend. I'm carrying the PDF and the research on Sequent AI, and I'll get those to you. Text me if anything shifts or if you want to talk through the partnership piece once you've had a chance to sit with it.

Talk soon, Royce.
All right, thank you.
